title: ECRO trained and rendered on the WL84 scene with the learned-ER closure as LOW material (D = 6)
authorization: User (research owner), 2026-11-18: train (if needed) and render the WL84 dataset (learned-ER results) with the current ECRO. Decisions: local RTX 5080 (inputs copied read-only from LabServer63); LOW material = learned ER (WL84 ER_L, compiler seed 8301); keep D = 6 and render new references (6-event and full depth), the WL84 depth-4 reference only as context; scope = the three WL84 images, with error maps.
class: Regular WL104 (new workload: training and evaluation of the existing ECRO architecture); numbered by the assistant under AGENTS.md, the owner may reclassify
machine: local RTX 5080 16 GB (desktop display shares the GPU), external/8dna26/.venv-cu128: Python 3.11.9, torch 2.8.0+cu128, Mitsuba 3.5.1 / Dr.Jit 0.4.6 (WL100 local stack)
inputs_note: Copied byte-for-byte from LabServer63 (~/rest_compiled83, ~/rest_compiled84); sha256 equal to the server originals (spot-checked, 5 files). Root results/ecro_wl84_104/inputs63/.

scene.definition: render81.scene_dict pose 0: floor 6 x 6 m and back wall 6 x 3 m (white Lambert 0.8), sphere centre (-0.4, 0, 0.35) r 0.35 and cube (0.45, 0.1, 0.25) yaw 35 deg half 0.25 with the image material; point light L1 (-1.5, -1.5, 2.5) I 25 or L2 (2.0, -0.6, 0.45) I 12; WL81 camera origin (0, -3, 1.2) target (0, 0, 0.3) fov 40, 256 x 256, pixel centre + uniform jitter.
scene.mesh_conversion: Every surface is a triangle mesh for the ECRO adapter and for ALL new arms and references: floor / wall = two-triangle quads with the Mitsuba rectangle frame; sphere = fixed UV sphere 128 x 256 (32,514 vertices, 65,024 faces, exact vertex positions and normals). This is the only scene change vs WL84; gate G2 measures it.
scene.materials: lay81 descriptor = materials83.npz[set][k]; learned-ER state = closure83_dr.compiled_state('ER', closure82.decode('ER', 'cert', z_k of fit_<set>_L_ER_s8301.npz)); state sha256 must equal WL84 audit84.json ER_L

ecro.architecture: ECRO v0 unchanged (model86.py, 735,664 parameters); WL102 mesh adapter (pt102, mesh102) unchanged; physical dispatcher = the scene BSDF = cmp83 learned-ER closure on sphere / cube, Mitsuba diffuse 0.8 on floor / wall; camera rays from the WL81 formula; D = 6 (events 1-2 path traced, events 3-6 from the learned table read at the second hit).
ecro.encoder_rows: One 69-float row per patch (PMAT = patch id, WL102): floor / wall = WL100 lambert(0.8); sphere / cube = the learned-ER compiled state itself (the native ECRO material row).
ecro.patch_layout: WL102 rule (25 cm cells, 6-way dominant normal, exact clipping): N = 991 in development (gate G4: N < 32768).
ecro.models: One model per material (3), each trained only on its material's dataset.
ecro.dataset: WL102 split sizes and light rule: train 128 items x 4 white point lights (ECRO fixture intensity) x 64 spp fields; val 16 x 4 x 2 halves x 128 spp; test 1 item = the two WL84 lights L1, L2 at 2 x 256 spp (table-level only, never trained on). Lights uniform in the room-side box [-3, 3] x [-3, 1.5] x [0, 3] m (in front of the one-sided back wall; pre-freeze smoke finding: lights behind it give all-zero targets and a 0/0 loss), >= 0.15 m clearance along 26 directions, not inside closed meshes, rejected within 0.3 m of L1 and L2; an all-zero target light stops generation; seeds 104100 / 104200 (the same light draws for every material). The generator is linear in the source, so training and evaluation intensities need not match.
ecro.training: train102.main unchanged (WL100 recipe: WL92A OWN loss, Adam 1e-3 -> 1e-5 cosine, warm-up 500, clip 10, 24,000 steps, final step, no selection), area input floor 0, seed 10401. Frozen collapse rule: final validation whole_rel_l1 >= 0.95 -> retry with seed 10501, then 10601; every attempt reported; all collapsed -> STOP.
ecro.evaluation: Per image: source s for the WL84 point light (exact pt86 NEE source), table B, ECRO frames 20 x 4 spp (seeds 104500 + 1000 i + q), 8 x 64 spp (104520 + 1000 i + q), 2 x 1024-spp halves (104540 + 1000 i + q).

references.renderer: WL84 render84.render_g (Mitsuba 'path', rr_depth 64, GPU rays with the WL81 camera, float64 across launches), mesh scene, two independent halves
references.LAY65: layered lay81, max_depth 65, 2 x 32768 spp: FINAL physical reference
references.LAY4: layered, max_depth 4, 2 x 16384 (gate G2 against the WL84 analytic-scene depth-4 reference)
references.ER7: learned-ER, max_depth 7, 2 x 32768 (G3 partner; ECRO-material 6-event reference)
references.ER65: learned-ER, max_depth 65, 2 x 32768 (Learned-ER path tracing at full depth = the WL84 method without truncation)
references.ER65_64: learned-ER, max_depth 65, 8 independent 64-spp renders (the WL84 ER_L operating point at full depth)
references.PTC: ECRO tracer (pt102 'cam' mode, D = 6, learned-ER), 2 x 4096 spp, components e1, e2, h (physical HIGH = events 3..6)
references.WL84_context: WL84 65,536-spp depth-4 references (analytic scene), the stored WL83 ER_L 64-spp render and 8 WL84 replicates, compared only with their own depth-4 reference

gates.G0: every copied input sha256 equals this protocol; the three learned-ER state hashes equal WL84 audit84.json; scene PLY hashes equal this protocol
gates.G1: adapter camera rays (pixel centres) equal the WL81 formula: max |direction difference| <= 1e-6
gates.G2: per image, object mask: rel L1(LAY4 mesh mean, WL84 analytic ref84) <= 1.5 x the noise-only expectation 0.866 x rel L1(ref84A, ref84B), and |object mean ratio - 1| <= 0.005
gates.G3: per image: ECRO tracer PTC (D = 6) vs Mitsuba ER7: object rel L1 <= 1.5 x 0.5 x hypot(rel L1 of the PTC halves, rel L1 of the ER7 halves); object and full-frame mean ratios within 1 %
gates.failure: Any gate failure stops the chain. A gate failure from an adapter defect may be corrected only by a labelled execution amendment approved by the owner; thresholds are never relaxed.

analysis.masks: render81.masks on the mesh scene (center rays): obj = sphere + cube; highlight = obj and luminance(LAY65) >= 3 x its object median; grazing = obj and |n . d| <= 0.25; full frame
analysis.metrics: Against LAY65: relative L1 (full, obj, highlight, grazing), relative RMSE (full, obj), luminance mean ratios; multi-seed arms averaged with SD over seeds. Arms: ECRO 4 spp, ECRO 64 spp, ECRO converged, Learned-ER PT full depth 64 spp and converged, Learned-ER PT 6-event and layered PT 6-event converged.
analysis.decomposition: Converged rel L1: representation = ECRO vs ER7; HIGH only = learned hl vs PTC h; LOW check = ECRO e1+e2 vs PTC e1+e2; material = ER7 vs LAY7; truncation = LAY7 vs LAY65; full-depth material = ER65 vs LAY65; total = ECRO vs LAY65. Reference noise from half differences.
analysis.wl84_context: WL83 ER_L 64 spp and WL84 replicates vs ref84 (depth 4), object and WL84-style highlight mask
analysis.error_maps: Per image: image, absolute and signed luminance error vs LAY65 (the WL84 row vs its own reference) for every arm; decomposition maps; ONE absolute error scale for all maps of WL104 = the largest |error| among them (M), logarithmic display sign(x) log(1 + |x|/m0) / log(1 + M/m0) with m0 = M/1000 so that converged errors stay visible next to 4-spp noise, real-unit colorbars (user preference: absolute shared scale, nonlinear display); display tone (e x / (1 + e x))^(1/2.2) with e = 1 / 99.5th percentile of reference luminance
analysis.timing: Descriptive only (desktop GPU): table generation parts, ECRO frame walls, Learned-ER PT 64-spp wall and GPU time
analysis.verdict: No adoption or superiority verdict. The report states measured fidelity and its decomposition; comparisons with path tracing are labelled path-traced re-rendering with the same learned-ER material.
